proposal:
STATUS: no universal polynomial total-state bound is obtained. Below is one repair, its per-state cost, and the exact place it stops.

1. Invariant already available (worth a Lean check): along any branch, restriction, Canon and accepted ELIM never increase clause count. So every retained state has at most m clauses of width at most n, and total work = poly(n,m) × (sum over levels of retained states). The state count is the only unbounded quantity.

2. Proposed repair Canon+ (NOT part of tested E-MRA). At root and in every branch, iterate to fixpoint: UP; build the implication graph of the binary clauses; Tarjan SCC in O(n+m); if a literal and its negation share an SCC, kill the state; otherwise substitute each literal by the least-index representative of its SCC, delete tautologies and duplicates, run subsumption. Then ELIM as now. Each productive round removes a variable, so at most n rounds; about O(n²m²) per state with naive subsumption. Substitution adds no clauses, so invariant 1 survives. History: append the literal map (v := ±rep) to the survivor's history like a DP reconstruction record; merging keeps the survivor's history intact.

3. Hand prediction on Neon's 32-clause formula (untested): variables 3..12 collapse to one variable x, leaving (-1,x),(1,2,x),(1,-2,x). ELIM on 2, then 1, yields unit x: SAT at root, zero branches.

4. Non-regression safeguard. Neon's example shows an added reduction can raise the peak, so 'Canon+ is never worse' is not claimed. Instead dovetail plain MRA, E-MRA and E-MRA+Canon+ in equal work slices and stop at the first to finish. Total work is at most 3× the best of the three by construction. This replaces the false H2 with a trivial but true work bound.

5. Potential and first unproved claim. Φ_k = number of Canon+-distinct, dominance-incomparable residuals at level k. Claim C1: residuals with equal binary part and equal non-binary clauses modulo its SCC classes get identical Canon+ forms. I expect this to be routine (deterministic representatives), but it is unproved and covers only binary-visible equivalence. Claim C2 (Φ_k polynomial on all inputs) I believe is false; see self_attack.

6. Fixture (ACTUAL unchanged E-MRA only). It keeps Neon's 25-clause core. Selector 2 is Neon's formula after its root elimination of variable 1. Selector 1 is the mirror image under the core automorphism (reverse arrows, negate, swap {3,4} with {11,12} and {5,6,7} with {8,9,10}). The core forces 3..12 equal; selector 2 forces that value true, selector 1 false: UNSAT. By hand I checked all 12 root, 22 level-one and 40 level-two elimination trials: each increases clause count (smallest margin +1), there are no units and no 2-CNF state. Four pairwise incomparable residuals survive variables 1,2 and all die at variable 3. Prediction: peak 4, 14 branch attempts. Caveats: the input has 4-literal clauses, and the hand simulation may err. Purpose: test whether hidden-equivalence blindness compounds multiplicatively; 2^k for k selectors is a conjecture needing larger cores. Under Canon+ (untested) the formula collapses to (2,x),(-2,x),(1,-x),(-1,-x) and is refuted at root.
missing_theorem: Wanted universal lemma U: there is a polynomial p such that for every CNF F with n variables and m clauses, under an order computable in polynomial time, the sum over k of Φ_k is at most p(n,m). U is not established. For any scheme that keeps one residual CNF per state and prunes only by implication, I conjecture U is false (Tseitin argument in self_attack). The weakest statement that would still give an all-input bound is U′: a class of objects, each representing a UNION of residuals (as affine cosets do for parity), with a polynomial emptiness test, closure under branching and ELIM, and polynomially many objects per level on every input. I know no candidate class; exhibiting one is the open problem itself, not a lemma. Checkable sublemmas within reach: (a) invariant 1; (b) Canon+ soundness and reconstruction; (c) C1; (d) the 3× dovetail work bound.
self_attack:
(i) Canon+ sees only binary implications. Equivalences entailed through wider clauses are invisible, for example an implication replaced by a gadget whose auxiliary variables each have 3×3 occurrences so ELIM rejects them; the same doubling should reappear. UP-entailment (failed-literal) pruning pushes this one step at about O(nm) per literal. But deciding residual equivalence in general is coNP-hard: a canonical form merging all equivalent residuals would map every unsatisfiable residual to one form and so decide SAT. Stronger merging therefore cannot supply a universal bound.
(ii) Even perfect semantic merging plus perfect implication pruning appears to fail (to be independently verified). Take a satisfiable Tseitin parity system on a bounded-degree expander. Assigning any half of the edge variables leaves residual affine systems indexed by boundary charge vectors. Distinct satisfiable ones are disjoint cosets, hence pairwise incomparable, and I expect 2^{Ω(n)} of them under every order. DP elimination should be count-increasing there. So Φ would be exponential on that family unless states stop being single residuals.
(iii) Canon+ changes ELIM's occurrence products and may block an elimination that previously succeeded. Only the dovetail bound protects against this, and it bounds work, not peak.
(iv) The fixture prediction rests on 74 hand-checked trials; one missed subsumption changes the peak. The checker may also reject 4-literal clauses. The 2^k extrapolation is untested.
(v) Nothing here bears on P versus NP; finite fixtures prove no general bound.
